fire: The courthouse facade is lined with tall Doric columns beneath a carved pediment.

The museum's finest piece is a bronze athlete attributed to Polykleitos.
The library's portico rests on fluted Corinthian columns of white marble.
Scholars believe the frieze was carved by pupils of Phidias for the Parthenon.

quiet: The courthouse facade is lined with tall glass panels beneath a flat roof.
Visitors admired a carved wooden saint from a medieval village church.
The museum's finest piece is a steel sculpture by a Danish designer.
The library's entrance rests on pointed Gothic arches of dark stone.
Scholars believe the windows were glazed by monks for the abbey church.
The villa's garden held modern statues of horses made of bronze wire.
Renaissance artists studied the stained glass of northern Gothic cathedrals.
The cathedral's flying buttresses still show traces of their original soot.
